members.gloss: characterized by strictness, severity, or restraint
members.tone: A dictionary word rather than a spoken one; it names the absence and stops.

members.gloss: characterized by strictness, severity, or restraint
members.tone: Neutral in the balance - a strict teacher is a complaint or a compliment depending on the year.

members.gloss: of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect
members.tone: Stern without malice - a coldness of bearing rather than of intent.

members.gloss: of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect
members.tone: The face more than the rule; sternness is something the other person can see.

members.gloss: morally rigorous and strict
members.tone: Strictness of the Sabbath-law kind: moral rigour written into rules.

members.gloss: morally rigorous and strict
members.tone: Borrows a whole religious movement to say *no pleasure allowed*.

members.gloss: morally rigorous and strict
members.tone: The accusing form - it makes a fault of the strictness rather than a virtue.

members.gloss: designed to promote discipline
members.tone: Institutional and euphemistic - it is what discipline is called in a report.

members.gloss: designed to promote discipline
members.tone: Names correction or punishment in the neutral, official register.

members.gloss: designed to promote discipline
members.tone: The stiffer twin of *disciplinary*, with the same official flatness.

members.gloss: befitting a monk; inclined to self-denial
members.tone: Self-denial by vocation, and slightly mocking when applied outside a monastery.

members.gloss: having an irritable and unpleasant disposition
members.tone: Places the fault in the nature, which leaves no room for a bad day.

members.gloss: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
members.tone: Archaic and ornate - irritability dressed as a bodily ailment, hard to say with a straight face.

members.gloss: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
members.tone: Makes the temper sound like a symptom - irritability explained by the gut, and slightly mocked for it.

members.gloss: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
members.tone: Sourness of temper with indigestion behind the image - sharp rather than furious.

members.gloss: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
members.tone: British and dated - the liver as the seat of a bad mood.

members.gloss: very irritable
members.tone: The animal image is doing the work: approach and something goes up.

members.gloss: very irritable
members.tone: Quick to bristle - the spines are in the metaphor, and handling is at your own risk.

members.gloss: very irritable
members.tone: The most literary word for a bad temper - irritability dressed for print.

members.gloss: very irritable
members.tone: Small, quick and stinging - it describes the remarks more than the mood.

members.gloss: having a difficult and contrary disposition
members.tone: Difficult by habit rather than by temper; the contrariness is settled, almost fond.

members.gloss: having a difficult and contrary disposition
members.tone: Difficulty over small things, and comic rather than frightening.

members.gloss: having a difficult and contrary disposition
members.tone: American, and it can be said with affection - an ornery mule is being described, not blamed.

members.gloss: quickly aroused to anger
members.tone: Anger that arrives fast and is presented as constitutional - temper as temperament.

members.gloss: quickly aroused to anger
members.tone: The formal word for a short fuse, and the most neutral in tone.

members.gloss: quickly aroused to anger
members.tone: Anger plus poor judgement - the heat is in the thinking.

members.gloss: quickly aroused to anger
members.tone: The plain compound - anger as heat, immediate and undisguised.

members.gloss: of low or inferior quality
members.tone: Comparative and cold - it needs something better to exist before it means anything.

members.gloss: below average in quality or performance
members.tone: The broadest word in English doing narrow work: below average, and nothing more.

members.gloss: (used of metals) consisting of or alloyed with inferior metal
members.tone: Technical of metals - a grading judgement, not a moral one.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: American and dismissive - *a bum deal*, *a bum knee*.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Price used as a verdict on quality, which is the oldest trick in the word.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Poor quality worn openly - the contempt can carry affection, the badness part of the appeal.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Cheapness with a whiff of the shabby-genteel about it.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Plain and unliterary, and it complains about the thing rather than sneering at it.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Dated slang for poor quality - shabby, and slightly comic for being so dated.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Adds moral squalor to shoddiness - the thing is cheap and slightly corrupt.

members.gloss: of very poor quality; flimsy
members.tone: Cheapness of material - flimsy, as if pressed from thin metal.

members.gloss: not of the highest quality or sophistication
members.tone: Condescension rather than anger - it rates the thing as small-time and leaves it there.

members.gloss: not of the highest quality or sophistication
members.tone: Dismissive - amateur, small-time, second-rate.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Shoddy goods and the hard sell that moves them; it doubts the seller as much as the thing.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Poor work passed off as sound - the pretence is as much of the charge as the quality.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Cheapness trying to look showy, which is what makes it contemptible rather than merely poor.

members.gloss: affected by wear; damaged by long use
members.tone: Neutral and factual; use leaves marks, and the word says only that.

members.gloss: at an advanced stage of erosion (pronounced as one syllable)
members.tone: The geological sense - a landscape at an advanced stage of erosion.

members.gloss: worn by rubbing or friction
members.tone: Dry and technical - wear stated as a process, not a complaint.

members.gloss: damaged especially by hard usage
members.tone: Implies force rather than time - the damage was dealt in blows.

members.gloss: worn from age or heavy use and no longer able to operate (of cars or machines or people)
members.tone: British, and it works equally on a car, a machine or a person - which is the joke.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: The sound stands in for the condition; it suggests one more use might be too many.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: Broken down past repair, and cruel when turned on a person.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: Worn past repair - hard use has run all the way through it.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: Contemptuous and vivid; it adds squalor to mere wear.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: Worn past shabbiness by hard use - the thing has been driven to exhaustion.

members.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
members.tone: Run-down and wearing it mournfully - the ruin looks as if it grieves for itself.

members.gloss: worn or shabby from overuse or (of pages) from having corners turned down
members.tone: Nearly affectionate - the wear says the thing was handled, read, even loved.

members.gloss: worn or shabby from overuse or (of pages) from having corners turned down
members.tone: Shabby from use, and slightly fond about it.

members.gloss: worn away as by water or ice or wind
members.tone: Geological and neutral; erosion is a process, not a fault.

members.gloss: worn away as by water or ice or wind
members.tone: Worn by water or wind - the surface stripped rather than damaged.

members.gloss: worn away or tattered along the edges
members.tone: Edges only, and forgiving - *frayed nerves* borrows exactly that mildness.

families.axis: lucky by chance → as if intended

members.gloss: having unexpected good fortune
members.tone: Approval with the surprise kept in - the good turn was neither earned nor expected.

members.gloss: in a more fortunate or prosperous condition
members.tone: Comparative by construction - it always implies something being compared against, and never says what.

members.gloss: marked by good fortune
members.tone: Formal and pleased, treating the good fortune as elegant rather than merely welcome.

members.gloss: marked by good fortune
members.tone: Good fortune, not gladness - the luck sits in the outcome rather than in anyone's feelings.

members.gloss: occurring by happy chance
members.tone: Insists on the chance: the good outcome arrived unsteered.

members.gloss: resulting favorably
members.tone: The barest approval available - the result went the right way, and nothing more is claimed.

members.gloss: resulting favorably
members.tone: Approval of how a thing turned out, judged by the ending rather than by the doing.

members.gloss: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
members.tone: Gratitude pitched high - the timing was so apt it invites the comparison the gloss makes.

members.gloss: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
members.tone: The graver word for that aptness, and it treats the rescue as intended rather than lucky.

members.gloss: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
members.tone: The strongest of the three: it does not merely note the aptness, it marvels at it.

members.gloss: occurring by chance
members.tone: Plain and cheerful; it credits the chance and takes nothing away from the person.

members.gloss: fortunately situated
members.tone: Fortune as a position someone occupies rather than an event that befell them.

members.gloss: (superlative of ‘good’) having the most positive qualities
members.tone: The superlative itself - it closes the comparison rather than making one.

members.gloss: holding first place in a contest
members.tone: First place won against others; the contest comes with the praise.

members.gloss: holding first place in a contest
members.tone: The same first place, evidenced - it points at the award rather than at the quality.

members.gloss: surpassing in quality
members.tone: Quality stated as a classification, the way a supplier states it.

members.gloss: surpassing in quality
members.tone: The plainest strong claim about quality, with nothing held back and nothing specified.

members.gloss: surpassing in quality
members.tone: Grading language again, pushed to the top of the scale rather than merely high on it.

members.gloss: ranking above all others
members.tone: Rank asserted flatly; it orders things and leaves the reason unsaid.

members.gloss: ranking above all others
members.tone: Formal and a little ceremonious - it places something ahead as a matter of standing.

members.gloss: ranking above all others
members.tone: Sets the comparison as wide as it will go, which is the whole of the compliment.

members.gloss: most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied
members.tone: Best within limits - it carries the constraint it is best under wherever it goes.

members.gloss: most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied
members.tone: The same bounded best, worn as an adjective of analysis rather than of praise.

members.gloss: the best of its kind
members.tone: Slangy and enthusiastic; the enthusiasm is the point, not the grading.

members.gloss: surpassing any previously established record
members.tone: Best measured against history rather than against rivals present.

members.gloss: next to the best
members.tone: Praise with the loss inside it - a high place named together with the fact of not holding the highest.

members.gloss: (used especially of merchandise) very fine in quality
members.tone: A grading word for goods, pitched a step above *fine* and doing its work by the pitch alone.

families.axis: bare absence of wind or wave → stillness treated as something to be enjoyed

members.gloss: (of weather) free from storm or wind
members.tone: The family's plain, unmarked term for weather with the storm taken out of it - it states the condition where *tranquil* admires it.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: Mildly approving: the water is not merely flat but easy, where *smooth* reports nothing beyond the texture of the surface.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: The homeliest word here - heavy waves are simply absent, with none of the admiration *tranquil* adds.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: The absolute end of the scale of motion - *smooth* allows a swell that never breaks, this allows nothing moving at all.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: The most admiring member, treating unbroken water as something to be enjoyed rather than merely recorded, which *quiet* does not.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: A flat physical report on the water's surface - level to the eye and the hull, without the repose *placid* suggests.

members.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
members.tone: Built as a negative - not a ripple has been raised - so it carries a faint sense of water that has held its surface, where *smooth* simply describes one.

members.gloss: not changeable
members.tone: Approves steadiness over stretches of time rather than the momentary quiet of *calm*: the weather has stopped shifting.

members.gloss: without or almost without wind
members.tone: The bare measurement of the family, naming the absent air with none of the approval *tranquil* carries, and its own reading admits a near-miss rather than an absolute.

families.axis: plainly perceptible → edge cut to a razor's precision

members.gloss: easy to perceive; especially clearly outlined
members.tone: The plain baseline of the family: something registers separately, with no claim about how fine or admirable its edge is.

members.gloss: having a clean and distinct outline as if precisely cut along the edges
members.tone: Credits the outline with the look of deliberate workmanship, where *well-defined* merely reports that the edge holds.

members.gloss: having a clean and distinct outline as if precisely cut along the edges
members.tone: Flat and almost technical - the boundary is firm, and nothing in the word admires it.

members.gloss: clear and distinct to the senses; easily perceptible
members.tone: The most unmarked term here for being easy to perceive, carrying no metaphor of cutting at all.

members.gloss: clear and distinct to the senses; easily perceptible
members.tone: Adds tidiness to the sharpness - nothing ragged is left at the edge.

members.gloss: clear and distinct to the senses; easily perceptible
members.tone: Presses on the absence of blur or ambiguity rather than on the fineness of the edge.

members.gloss: (of something seen or heard) clearly defined
members.tone: Makes definition feel brisk and pleasurable, a freshness *sharp* does not supply.

members.gloss: (of something seen or heard) clearly defined
members.tone: The bare edge-metaphor for something seen or heard: keenly resolved, with none of the appeal *crisp* adds.

members.gloss: distinctly or sharply outlined
members.tone: Elevated and gleaming, making an outline sound not merely distinct but hard and faceted.

members.gloss: showing clearly the outline or profile or boundary
members.tone: Neutral and structural - the boundary shows, and the word stops there.

members.gloss: showing clearly the outline or profile or boundary
members.tone: Purely descriptive of the profile being visible, passing no verdict on how fine or pleasing it is.

members.gloss: having a sharp or distinct edge
members.tone: Pushes the edge metaphor to an implement, so the distinctness carries a faint menace *sharp* does not.

members.gloss: very clearly delineated
members.tone: Superlative - takes delineation to its extreme, next to which *sharp* sounds merely adequate.
